mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of residence of each individual

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid business license / certificate of registration of the foreign corporate General Partner (e.g., Chinese business license issued by SAMR)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification and verification of all partners, directors, officers, and individuals with significant control (ISC) at the 25% threshold; mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all such persons against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (Global Affairs Canada), the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and, for all USD-denominated transactions, the OFAC SDN List; mandatory risk classification for foreign politically exposed persons, domestic politically exposed persons, and heads of international organizations per FINTRAC guidance, with enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval where a PEP is identified; screening must be completed before any capital contribution or bank onboarding and is recommended to continue on an ongoing basis for the life of the partnership; enforcement authorities include FINTRAC, the RCMP, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for federally regulated financial institutions, and the Alberta Director of Corporate Registries.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry — NUANS name search and name pre-reservation ordered through authorized corporate registry service providers using the Alberta Corporate Registration System (ACRS); official registration filings submitted via Service Alberta's Corporate Registry (www.albertaregistries.ca / www.servicealberta.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta limited partnership names must be expressed in English or French alphabetic characters (Roman/Latin script); numerals may appear in figures or words; permitted punctuation is limited to apostrophe, comma, hyphen, period, and ampersand. Non-Latin script names (e.g., Chinese characters) must be transliterated into Latin characters or replaced with a distinctive English or French name, with certified transliteration where the foreign corporate General Partner's underlying name is in a non-Latin script. The legal element 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'LP', or 'société en commandite' is mandatory.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Trustco, Insurance, Assurance, Loan, Finance, Financial, Lender, Broker, Mortgage (financial-services tokens requiring prior regulatory consent)
Royal, Crown, Queen, King, Prince, Government, Federal, National, Municipal, Department (Crown or governmental connotation prohibited)
University, College, Institute, Academy, Hospital (regulated or public-institution connotation)
Co-operative, Credit Union, Savings, Deposit (reserved for alternative statutory entity forms)
Chartered, Certified, Engineer, Architect, Lawyer, Doctor (professional designation requiring statutory qualification)
Obscene, scandalous, insulting, or publicly offensive words and designs (absolute statutory prohibition)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If name clearance is refused, the applicant may: (1) file a written name-review request within 30 days to the Director of Corporate Registries, Service Alberta, attaching the refusal notice, a fresh NUANS search report if the prior report has expired, evidence of distinctiveness, and any written consent obtained from an existing name holder; (2) obtain and file a signed consent letter from the confusingly similar name holder where commercially feasible; (3) if the Director upholds the refusal, apply for judicial review to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 2 months of the final decision under applicable administrative-law remedies; (4) concurrently clear an alternative name and proceed with limited partnership registration, then file a Declaration of Change of Name once an acceptable name is obtained. Mere delay does not extend the 90-day reservation window; a new reservation and NUANS search fee are required after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted. Alberta registries accept a licensed registered agent's physical street address as the limited partnership's registered office, and full-time staff presence at that address is not required; however, a P.O. box or pure mail-forwarding virtual office with no physical street address is prohibited. For a cross-dock and overseas 3PL warehouse operator, active commercial substance requires a dedicated physical warehouse and operations address in Alberta, and a purely virtual registered office without operational premises will not satisfy CRA, Alberta Treasury Board and Finance, banking counterparties, or CBSA expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate. Approximately 30% probability of an unannounced municipal business-licence or Alberta OHS inspection within the first 24 months of active warehousing operations; approximately 15-20% annual probability of a CRA GST/HST field audit for a standard-risk registrant; approximately 20-30% probability of a CBSA physical inventory inspection if the warehouse stores imported goods, duty-deferred goods, or operates as a customs-bonded facility.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 3 (Limited Partnerships), as amended; sections concerning registration, powers of general partners, and certification.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by Alberta law for a limited partnership; capital contributions are determined by the limited partnership agreement and may be in cash, property, or other value. No statutory escrow or paid-up capital deposit obligation applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Limited Partnership Agreement is approved; each partner hereby subscribes to the capital contributions set forth in Schedule A. RESOLVED that the registered office is established at the address shown in the Declaration of Limited Partnership, and the Registrar is authorized to accept service of legal process under the Partnership Act. RESOLVED that the General Partner appoints [Name] as Managing Partner, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer, each serving until removal. RESOLVED that such officers are authorized to execute and file the Declaration of Limited Partnership, make all government filings, open banking accounts, and engage the initial lease and operating permits necessary to commence business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search to confirm the proposed limited partnership name is distinguishable from existing names in Alberta. Submit a name reservation request to the Alberta Corporate Registry if immediate reservation is desired.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit an alternative name or obtain a written consent from the existing name holder permitting the similarity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Limited Partnership Agreement and Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the limited partnership agreement specifying capital contributions, profit-sharing, management authority, admission and withdrawal of partners, dissolution events, and dispute resolution. Complete the Declaration of Limited Partnership on the prescribed form, stating the limited partnership's name, registered office address in Alberta, full names and addresses of all general partners, and a statement of initial capital contributions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar queries a defect in the draft declaration, revise the document and resubmit within the statutory response period, or obtain legal opinion to clarify ambiguous terms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Registration of the Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed Declaration of Limited Partnership, together with the prescribed filing fee and any required consents, to the Alberta Corporate Registry either online or by mail. Verify that the declaration is signed by each general partner and witnessed as required by the Partnership Act.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Declaration of Limited Partnership
Identification and consent of each general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, correct the deficiencies listed in the notice of rejection and resubmit; if the issue involves a legal defect, amend the declaration or file a corrected declaration with supporting legal opinion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Certificate of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Limited Partnership confirming the creation of the limited partnership. Verify all details, including name, registration number, date of registration, and registered office address. Request a certified copy or consolidated extract for banking, leasing, and contracting purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or registry extract contains errors, file a Notice of Correction with the Registry or request an administrative correction under the Partnership Act procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax and Business Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Alberta Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for the federal Business Number, GST/HST account if sales exceed the threshold, payroll account if employees are expected, and import/export account if cross-border trading occurs. For Alberta, obtain any provincial tax or program registrations as needed. Update the registered office and partner information with the Alberta Corporate Registry as changes occur.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA account registration is delayed, contact the CRA business help line or use the CRA online portal to track and expedite processing; for provincial registrations, contact Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration for guidance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Planning and Development Department (designated by the registered office municipality)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence for Warehousing and Cross-Dock Logistics

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Screening level (full EIA not required for a cross-dock warehouse; environmental site assessment may be requested if suspected contamination)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Stormwater and wastewater discharges must comply with Alberta's Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act and applicable municipal effluent limits; VOC and diesel particulate emissions from warehouse equipment must meet provincial air quality regulations and the National Emissions Standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety permit and inspection by the local fire department; building occupancy certification under the Alberta Fire Code; structural load plans certified by a licensed engineer; workplace hazard clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (Alberta).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) acting as the central tax administration; online portals include CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account. Provincial entity registration for an Alberta Limited Partnership is administered by the Alberta Corporate Registry. Alberta does not impose a provincial sales tax or separate VAT; corporate income tax for Alberta is collected by the CRA under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act collection agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Alberta LP must first be registered or extra-provincially registered with the Alberta Corporate Registry. For tax identity, the LP's general partner or authorized representative files Form RC1 Request for a Business Number with the CRA electronically via Business Registration Online or by mail/fax. The application requires the LP legal name, Alberta registration number, principal business activity (NAICS 493110), names and addresses of all partners, and a request for a GST/HST program account. Non-resident partners should supply their foreign tax identification numbers; if there is no Canadian-resident general partner, a resident agent for service must be designated. The CRA assigns a nine-digit Business Number and separate program accounts (e.g., RM, RP, RT, RC) with appropriate effective dates.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. An Alberta LP is fiscally transparent under the Income Tax Act; income is computed at partnership level and allocated to partners. Available elections include a partnership non-calendar fiscal period election, a section 216 election for non-resident partners, and a joint election for nil consideration on supplies between closely related registrants for GST/HST purposes. Hybrid mismatch rules under sections 18.2 and 18.3 impose deduction limitations and do not offer elective relief.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) — Alberta is not a participating HST province, so only the federal 5% GST applies to taxable supplies of warehousing and fulfillment services in Alberta.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the small supplier threshold computed on worldwide revenue from taxable supplies (other than zero-rated supplies) made in Canada over the preceding four calendar quarters; registration is compulsory once exceeded, and voluntary registration is available to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous electronic authentication of GST/HST invoices. Registrants must issue paper or electronic invoices containing prescribed particulars, including the Business Number, date, recipient identity, description and tax amount, and must retain records for six years. Exports require CBSA electronic export declarations via Canadian Government EDI or the appropriate CBSA portal; no digital stamp is applied.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods is zero-rated when the goods are exported by the seller in compliance with ETA Schedule VI, Part V, Section 1 and CRA proof-of-export rules. Services supplied to a non-resident are zero-rated under Section 9/10 only when the service is not performed in respect of Canadian real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance. Therefore warehousing and fulfillment services performed on inventory physically located in Canada are generally taxable at 5% GST even when the recipient is a non-resident; a separately contracted international freight forwarding leg may be zero-rated if structured and documented as a distinct supply of transportation from Canada to a foreign destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA B13A Export Declaration or approved electronic export report for goods valued at CAD 2,000 or more
Bill of Lading or air waybill showing the foreign destination
Proof of export retained in records, including carrier evidence and customs release documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA will deny zero-rating and reassess the supply at 5% GST plus interest and penalties where documentary export proof is insufficient or not obtained within the applicable prescribed time. Civil penalties include a false-statement penalty equal to the greater of CAD 100 and a percentage of the misstatement (often up to 25%), gross-negligence penalties, and potential criminal prosecution for deliberate evasion. Input tax credits connected to Canadian warehouse expenses can be retrospectively disallowed and recovered, with a general four-year reassessment period extended to six years for neglect, carelessness, or wilful default.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the sole issuing and monetary authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as prudential regulator of Schedule I banks under the Bank Act; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the AML/CFT supervisory authority under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canada operates no dedicated foreign-exchange-control administration; residual authority derives from the Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, the Bank Act, and PCMLTFA reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains unrestricted current- and capital-account convertibility as an Article VIII member of the IMF; there is no licensing, approval, or quota system governing capital injections, profit remittances, or foreign-currency account holding. The CAD trades under a free float. The only compliance frictions for an Alberta Limited Partnership are: (i) Part XIII non-resident withholding on distribution of Canadian-source income allocations to non-resident partners (25% statutory, treaty-reducible), which affects repatriation structuring rather than convertibility; (ii) CDD/UBO disclosure at account opening; (iii) mandatory FINTRAC reporting of cross-border electronic transfers of CAD 10,000 or more; and (iv) Statistics Canada balance-of-payments reporting via the servicing bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion ratio on export proceeds; exporters may retain, invoice, and disburse in any currency. Statutory obligations are confined to transparency: (i) CBSA export reporting via B13A/CAED for commercial shipments exceeding the low-value threshold (approximately CAD 2,000 per shipment), due within 15 calendar days after the month of export, with e-commerce low-value parcels generally exempt; (ii) Statistics Canada balance-of-payments returns for goods/services flows through the servicing bank (threshold-based monthly surveys); and (iii) FINTRAC cross-border EFT reporting for any transfer of CAD 10,000 or more.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Multi-Currency Operational Account (CAD/USD) with FX overlay
Operational Current Account with USD sub-ledger and cross-border sweep
Operational Account with USD Clearing Account and commercial LC facility
Operational Account for CAD retail clearing and trade disbursements
Operational Account with FX hedging line and Asia/Latin America correspondent reach
Capital Escrow / Operational Account for Alberta-domiciled entities
Operational Account for secondary CAD liquidity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability for operational last-mile disbursement: Airwallex, Wise Business, and Payoneer operate in Canada as FINTRAC-registered Money Services Businesses under the PCMLTFA, supporting US ACH, UK FPS, EU SEPA, and China local e-payment rails with favorable FX spreads and rapid settlement. Medium-to-Low viability for capital escrow and high-value clearing: non-bank EMIs lack OSFI prudential supervision and CDIC deposit insurance, and Schedule I banks will not treat EMI references as sufficient source-of-funds evidence. Recommended architecture: Schedule I chartered bank as the liquidity anchor for capital, clearing, and derivatives; fintech EMI overlay restricted to documented settlement-friction reduction with an audited payment-flow matrix.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally available under FINTRAC dual-process identity verification (electronic credential validation or video interview), but Schedule I banks in practice require: (i) video KYC interviews for General Partner directors/officers; (ii) certified true copies of the Alberta Partnership Registration Certificate, LP Agreement, and GP constitutional documents; (iii) notarized identification, proof-of-address, and bank reference letters for non-resident directors and UBOs; and (iv) source-of-funds dossiers for capital contributions. Physical branch attendance is not an absolute statutory mandate for RBC/TD/BMO/CIBC; it is persistently requested by ATB Financial and by private-banking units for non-resident UBOs. Fully remote onboarding typically completes in 2–3 weeks; hybrid in-person closings complete in 3–6 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity through nested General Partner layers and silent limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Partnership Registration Certificate; current Register of Partners; executed LP Agreement with contribution schedule; UBO declaration forms tracing through every corporate GP tier to ultimate natural persons; corporate registry extracts for each GP entity; group organizational chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partner concentration and capital injection from low-substance jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-partner source-of-funds and source-of-wealth files (bank statements, tax returns, disposition contracts); PEP/sanctions screening reports; tax-residency certificates; home-bank reference letters; economic-substance evidence (premises lease, staffing records, business plan).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity outbound payments to overseas 3PL warehouses in the US, Hong Kong, and China flagged as high-risk counterparty flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed 3PL warehouse service agreements; commercial invoices and packing lists; CBSA export declarations or low-value exemption evidence; carrier settlement reports; supplier KYC declarations; reconciliation of wire frequency to order-volume platform data.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly registered Alberta LP with no domestic revenue footprint receiving a rapid, large initial capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-office lease or shared-office agreement; Alberta provincial registration; capital-call schedule linking LP Agreement to wire timing; projected treasury cash-flow model; escrow-to-operational transfer sequence documentation; counterparty bank verification of each remitter.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign partners remit by SWIFT MT103 to the LP's capital-escrow or operational account at the Schedule I bank. The field-70 remittance narrative must classify the flow as a direct-investment equity contribution (IMF BOP direct-investment category), e.g., 'LP Capital Contribution — [partner], [date], per LP Agreement §[X]; no goods/services consideration', matching the bank's BOP mapping code. The LP pre-files a capital-verification packet (LP Agreement, capital-call notices, subscription schedules, partner CDD) before the first wire. Inbound transfers of CAD 10,000 or more trigger mandatory FINTRAC EFT reports; large values also enter Statistics Canada goods BOP returns. USD wires clear through the bank's US correspondent (RBC/TD/BMO New York branches) for same-day availability; CAD balances clear via Payments Canada Lynx.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Standard disbursement stack: (i) SWIFT MT103 wires for 3PL warehouse fees, last-mile carrier settlement, and ad-hoc vendor payments; (ii) commercial documentary Letters of Credit (UCP600, MT700/MT710) via the Schedule I bank for bulk inventory purchases routed to overseas warehouses; (iii) Payments Canada Lynx for high-value CAD real-time settlement and Retail Batch ACH for domestic operating expenses; (iv) USD wire through the bank's Fedwire/CHIPS clearing channel, with fintech overlay (Airwallex/Wise local rails — US ACH, UK FPS, EU SEPA, China local e-payment) for cost-effective last-mile payouts. All outbound cross-border EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more are FINTRAC-reportable; treasury must maintain a remittance ledger mapping each payment to warehouse agreement, invoice, and order lineage.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD, CNY/CAD where market-accessible) bilaterally executed with a Schedule I bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNH for Chinese warehouse payables via licensed offshore dealing desks
Cross-currency swaps exchanging principal and interest (USD funding to CAD operating liquidity) for matched asset-liability hedging
Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars on USD/CAD protecting repatriated partnership income from adverse conversion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Limited Partnership Annual Registration Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each calendar year under Alberta's Registration Renewal Program; not based on the formation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registration becomes expired on April 1; continuing activity under an expired registration may result in loss of contract enforcement rights, administrative cancellation, restoration fees, and prosecution under the Alberta Partnership Act and Business Names Registration Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 Slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following the calendar year in which the partnership fiscal period ends for December 31 year-ends; non-calendar fiscal periods require the CRA-published T5013 due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly penalty under the Income Tax Act per partner for late filing, additional per-slip penalties for late T5013 slips, and CRA administrative reassessment if partnership income is not reported.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST Return (if the Limited Partnership is a GST/HST registrant)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end for annual filers; quarterly or monthly filers follow their stated reporting period deadlines.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest, 5% late-filing penalty on unpaid balance plus 1% per month for up to 12 months, and CRA set-off or collection action for prolonged delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notice of Change for Alberta Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of a triggering event affecting partnership name, general partner, registered address, or partner status; not a calendar-year annual filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Outdated registry information may lead to administrative cancellation of registration, loss of court standing, and monetary penalties under Alberta partnership registration legislation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The Alberta Partnership Act does not impose a statutory audit threshold on limited partnerships. An independent audit becomes mandatory only when required by the limited partnership agreement, a lender or investor, a regulatory licence condition, or where the general partner corporation is otherwise required to appoint an auditor under the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is the default framework for a private Canadian limited partnership; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) applies if the partnership or a controlling partner is publicly accountable. Tax-basis reporting reconciles to the T5013 and CRA filing requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta limited partnerships are not yet subject to the province's corporate beneficial-ownership filing regime, which currently applies to Alberta corporations. The annual March 31 registration renewal is the required annual confirmation point for the general partner name and Alberta address. Any transfer of a partnership interest must be documented in the LP records, and a Notice of Change must be filed with Alberta Corporate Registry within the prescribed amendment period if the transfer affects registered particulars.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (limited and general partners, capital contributions and withdrawals)
Register of General Partner (name, jurisdiction, corporate status)
General Partner Minute Book (consent resolutions for asset and financing transactions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120-600 per annum for a non-resident limited partnership using an Alberta registered office and agent package; higher if the same agent files annual renewals and forwards regulatory correspondence.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000-35,000 for a full independent audit if triggered by a lender or regulatory condition; USD 5,000-10,000 for a review engagement used for partner reporting.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general corporate rate (15% federal + 8% Alberta provincial) applicable to corporate partners of the LP; reduced combined rate of 11% (9% federal small business + 2% Alberta small business) applies to Canadian-controlled private corporation partners on active business income up to CAD 500,000. The Alberta Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent; the statutory rate applies at the partner level under the Income Tax Act (Canada).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general provincial tax holiday exists in Alberta. Relevant incentives include: (1) federal small business deduction producing the 11% combined rate for CCPC partners; (2) accelerated CCA at 10% declining balance for eligible non-residential logistics buildings acquired before 2028 and used at least 90% for manufacturing/processing or storage of goods for sale; (3) temporary immediate expensing for eligible capital property acquired on or before December 31, 2027, subject to the CAD 1.5 million annual cap; (4) Alberta Investor Tax Credit up to 30% for eligible Alberta investments, generally unavailable to passive 3PL warehouse operators; (5) Clean Technology Investment Tax Credit of 30% for qualifying zero-emission energy equipment, unrelated to conventional warehousing.
